marl_greet: ^Another one through the gate after dark. Either you're lost, or somebody sent you to count our spears.
^He has not stood up. A sergeant who stays seated is telling you exactly what he thinks of you.
marl_hub: ^Why do you keep the bell under your roof?
^[Show him the strip of linen from the bell.]
^The commander wants me at the ford. I need a horse.
marl_who: ^Sergeant Marl. Thirty-one winters on this rock, and the rock is winning.
marl_place: ^A gate, a wall, and eleven men who argue about the soup. We watch the road north. The road has done nothing interesting since the old king died.
marl_bell: ^The last man who kept that bell in the rain let it rust silent. Ring it once for a rider, twice for trouble. Three times, and I'll want to know who taught you to count.
marl_offer: ^You want to be useful? There's a grey mare in my stable that I never let in. Saddle still steaming. And nobody rang that bell. Find out who came through my gate tonight.
^journal:rider:Marl wants to know who came through the gate tonight. There is a grey mare in his stable, and nobody rang the bell.
marl_progress: ^A horse doesn't open a gate by itself. Start with the stable. Then have a look at the bell.
marl_rag: ^That is kitchen linen, and greasy with it. There's only one woman on this rock who wipes her hands on everything she owns.
marl_bye: ^Mind the cart on your way out, and the cook as well. Mostly the cook.
marl_finale: ^He looks at you the way he looks at the road: waiting for it to do something.
^It was Hedda. She tied up the bell.
^I'll give it to the commander myself.
marl_letter: ^Recalled. The commander's recalled to the capital, and we're to be cut to six men. Six men, on a wall built for forty. Well. Now you know why nobody wanted that bell rung.
marl_only_hedda: ^journal:letter:I still carry the courier's letter. The commander lives in the tower on the cliff.
^Hedda. Of course it was Hedda. I'll have words with her. Short ones. She'll have longer ones for me.
marl_commander: ^journal:letter:I promised Tam the letter goes to the commander, in the tower on the cliff. Marl let me go, for now.
^You have the face of someone carrying more than they came in with. I'll not ask tonight. But I will ask.
^He let you keep it. He also let you see him decide to.
marl_nothing: ^journal:letter:I still carry the courier's letter. The commander lives in the tower on the cliff.
^You have the face of someone carrying more than they came in with. I'll not ask tonight. But I will ask.
marl_horse: ^A horse. For the ford. In this weather. The commander's idea, I suppose, and my mare. Bring her back with four legs and I'll forgive you the rest.
^journal:ferryman:Marl lent me his mare. The ford is two hours north in the rain. The ferryman will not be expecting company.
^He watches you go the way he watched the road all night: waiting for it to do something.
hedda_greet: ^Shut that door, you're letting the rain into my bread. Who let you in? No, don't tell me. Marl. Marl lets anything in.
hedda_again: ^She does not look up from the pot.
hedda_hub: ^[Hold up the greasy linen from the bell rope.]
hedda_who: ^Hedda. I cook. I've cooked for three commanders and buried two of them, and the third one won't eat his greens.
hedda_rider: ^Rider? What rider. I've been up to my elbows in pease since vespers. Did you see a rider? No. Then there wasn't one.
^Two bowls drying by the basin. A spoon still in one. She has not been eating alone.

b: ^She stops stirring. For a long moment she looks at you as if you had come in with mud on your boots and somehow not tracked it in.
^She laughs, a sound like a cart on gravel, and goes back to her pot.

hedda_confess: ^That's my linen. Fine. It was Tam, my sister's boy. He rides for the king's post, and he wouldn't let go of his letter, not even to eat.

^journal:rider:Hedda's nephew Tam brought a letter for the commander and asked her to keep the bell quiet. He sleeps under the timber watch hood by the north-west tower door, up the stair beside the cookhouse.
hedda_why: ^He begged me. Said the letter's for the commander's eyes, and if the bell rang, Marl would have it open before the boy got his boots off. So I tied it. One knot. I've tied worse on worse men.
hedda_where: ^Up the tower stair, in the watch hood, asleep with the satchel under his head like a pillow. Wake him, and I'll salt your soup till midsummer.
hedda_bye: ^Go on, then. And wipe your feet. This floor has seen more blood than you have, and it's still cleaner.

b: ^ Two stalls under a lean-to against the east wall, hay in the loft over the mangers, oat bin with a stone on the lid against rats. Two horses in tonight: the old bay, and a grey mare you have not seen before.
^ The grey mare has her head in the manger. The courier's saddle is still on her, the bags hanging empty.

look_stable: ^A grey mare stands in the second stall, lathered to the hocks, steam rising off her in the cold. A courier's saddle, the bags empty. In the straw under the stirrup, something small and red.
^New shoes, and a post-house brand on her shoulder. The king's post: she has been changed at every station and ridden hard between them.

c-0: ^Half a wax seal, broken clean. A tower over three wavy lines. Someone opened a letter here, or wanted it to look that way.
^journal:rider:Half a broken seal in the stable straw: a tower over three wavy lines. And still nobody rang the bell.
^The king's post carries the council's crown. Three waves is somebody else's seal.

b: ^ A bronze bell no bigger than a helmet, on a bracket above the watch shelter. The rope comes down through the roof boards to a knot at shoulder height. Once for a rider, twice for trouble.

look_bell: ^A bronze bell no bigger than a helmet. The rope no longer hangs to the knot at shoulder height: somebody has hitched it up to the bracket with a strip of cloth, well out of reach.
^The bracket is older than the shelter, older than the gate. This bell has been rung for riders since before your grandfather's grandfather. It has never been gagged.

c-0: ^A strip of linen, stiff with old fat and smelling of onions. Kitchen linen. The rope drops back to its knot.
^journal:rider:Someone hitched the bell rope out of reach with greasy kitchen linen. Who wipes their hands on linen like this?

look_cookhouse: ^A lean-to against the north-west tower: oven in front, hearth at the back under a stone hood. Beside it a stair climbs to the tower door. Bread, pease pottage, salt pork on feast days.
look_nw_tower_stair: ^Twenty-four steps of wet stone up the west curtain, worn to a dish in the middle of every tread, and no rail on the drop side. It starts at the flank of the cookhouse and ends at the north-west tower door, where a lamp is lit.

b: ^ Up on the landing by the tower door, a bundle of wet cloak that breathes.

tam_stranger: ^A young man asleep on the boards in a wet cloak, a satchel under his head. Somebody else's business, for now.

b: ^ He sleeps on, one hand on the empty satchel.

tam_asleep: ^He sleeps curled on the boards, a wet cloak over him, the satchel under his head like a pillow.
^The strap is loose. One hand rests on the buckle, not holding it.
^Ease the letter out of the satchel.
tam_slip_ok: ^Your hands are steady. The buckle gives without a sound and the letter slides out, its seal already broken: a tower over three wavy lines. Tam sleeps on.
^journal:rider:I have the courier's letter. Its seal was broken before it got here. What do I tell Marl?
tam_slip_fail: ^The buckle clicks like a crossbow. His eyes open.
tam_wake: ^Who's there? Don't touch that. It's for the commander, that is, and it was sealed when they gave it me. I swear it was.
tam_awake: ^Tam sits with his back to the door, hugging his knees, watching you.
tam_hub: ^I'll make sure the commander gets it.
tam_seal: ^It was broken at the ford. A man in a grey ferryman's cloak held my satchel while I watered the horse. When he gave it back, the wax was split.
^A ferryman at a ford, with time enough to read a letter. The fords belong to the Wardens of the Three Waters. So does that seal.
tam_hedda: ^Please, don't tell the sergeant. Aunt Hedda tied the bell for me. If anyone hangs for it, let it be me and not her.
^He means it. He also hopes you will not take him up on it.

b: ^He pulls the satchel closer and shakes his head. Not you, not yet.

tam_letter: ^Take it, then. I'm too tired to fight you and too scared to sleep. Only give it to the commander, will you? Not to Marl.
^journal:rider:Tam gave me the letter and asked me to bring it to the commander, not to Marl. Its seal was broken at the ford.
cmd_too_early: ^The commander is writing by candlelight. He lifts one finger without looking up: not now.
cmd_with_letter: ^Close the door behind you. The draught finds this room before it finds anyone else. People only climb my stair at night when they carry something.
^He has not slept. The candle has been trimmed three times; the wax on the desk says so.
cmd_who: ^He gives you his name as if it were a rank: Captain Orrin Vael. Nineteen winters commanding this gate.
cmd_read: ^So they recall me, after nineteen years. And six men left to hold a gate built for forty. Somebody in the capital has learned to count.
^He folds the letter along its old creases, very carefully, the way a man handles something that has already hurt him.
cmd_after_marl: ^Marl brought me a letter tonight, and a story about a stranger who found it. I assume the stranger is you. Stand by the fire, at least.
cmd_seal: ^This seal was broken before it reached me. Three waves. The Wardens' mark, not the council's crown. Tell me where it happened, and tell me exactly.
^At the ford. A ferryman held Tam's satchel while he watered the horse.
^Not in your stable. Before. On the road.

b: ^You start to explain and lose the thread somewhere between the stable and the bell. He waits. Then he does not.

cmd_reason_ok: ^The seal half in the straw was broken clean and cold: the wax had set long before the mare stood there. A letter opened on the road, resealed badly, and opened again here by nobody.
^Where on the road does a royal courier stop long enough? Water. A ford.
cmd_ask_tam: ^Then go and ask him. Gently. He is nineteen and frightened, and frightened people remember the wrong things.
^journal:letter:Captain Vael wants to know where the seal was broken. Tam, asleep on the north-west tower landing, would know.
cmd_ford: ^A ferryman at the ford. The Wardens take their tolls at that ford, and they have wanted this road unwatched for as long as I have watched it.
^I leave at first light, if I leave at all. Before then, find me that ferryman. Quietly. Marl will give you a horse if you ask him nicely.
^journal:ferryman:Captain Vael wants the ferryman from the ford found before first light, quietly. Marl will give me a horse.
cmd_identity: ^And you. Marl says you came to count our spears. If you did, count carefully. They are all we have left.
^He is not asking. He is giving you the chance to lie well.
cmd_claim_assessor: ^He nods once, as if a debt had been entered in the right column.
cmd_claim_lost: ^Lost men do not usually find letters. He lets it pass.

b: ^He looks away first. Something in his shoulders settles, as though silence were the first honest answer he has had all night.
^You blink. He sees it, and files it, and says nothing either.

cmd_bye: ^Go on. Mind the stair on your way down. The seventh step is a liar.
cmd_again: ^He is writing. He does not stop.
cmd_again_ferry: ^First light, he says, without looking up.
look_pot_rack: ^Four pots, a pan with a handle too long for any hearth in this garrison, two ladles and a string of sausages that the cook counts every morning. The onions are counted too. Hedda is careful with anything that can be eaten.
look_cat_seat: ^A plaited basket in the warm gap between hearth and oven, with half a sack folded into it and a dent in the middle the size of a curled-up cat. The bowl beside it is red clay and filled every evening.
^The milk is fresh. She feeds the cat before she feeds eleven men, and she would deny it under oath.
look_ledgers: ^The muster roll and the stores book, side by side. The roll has forty lines ruled in it, and eleven have a name. Under a river stone beside them lies a letter with a crown seal, a month old and unanswered.
^A month. He knew something was coming long before Tam rode in, and chose not to open the door to it.
look_map: ^The march painted on a board: the north road as one red line, the river as a blue one, the garrison a black tower where they nearly cross. Pin holes run along the road, one for every rider that came through.
^Where road meets river there is a ford, and somebody has pressed a thumbnail into the paint there until the board split.
look_shrine: ^A niche no bigger than a loaf, a carved saint in it and an oil lamp that is never let go out. The saint's face is rubbed smooth by thumbs.
^The niche is older than the tower. Somebody built a soldier's house around a prayer, and the stone has kept it.
look_window: ^A paired window, deep enough to sit in, a shutter folded back on each side. Outside there is nothing: the rock falls away into a valley full of mist and rain.
^Ten metres of dark air. Your stomach notices before you do. Breathe out. Step back.
